added.name: Mirrors
added.long_description:
Mirrors provides regression testing for AI agents.

Teams shipping agents constantly change prompts, models, and tools, and there's no way to test any of it. Agents call bespoke internal tools and APIs no test framework can reproduce, so most teams ship on vibes.

Mirrors rebuilds the tools your agent calls from your own production traces, then replays real sessions against every change before it merges. You see which tool calls changed, which arguments moved, and where state landed differently. And when something fails, we tell you whether your agent regressed or something upstream moved.

Built for teams whose agents take irreversible actions. Refunds, record updates, outbound email.

Runs in your CI on every PR.
added.one_liner: Catch and fix AI agent regressions before they reach production

added.name: DeepMark
added.long_description: DeepMark is the authentication layer for AI voice. When an AI agent speaks, we embed a compact, machine-readable ID directly into the audio, not in metadata, which gets stripped the moment a file is touched. The ID resolves to a trust record, so a bank, a call center, or the person on the line can verify in real time who the agent is.

long_description.before:
Haystack helps engineering teams manage the growing volume of AI-generated pull requests.

Coding agents make it much easier to produce code, but they also create a new problem: teams now have more changes to review, many of them larger, more frequent, and harder to trust at a glance.

Haystack sits on top of GitHub and acts as the control layer for AI-generated code changes. For every pull request, it looks at the codebase, the diff, the agent trace, the author’s intent, and any verification evidence like tests, logs, commands, or screenshots.

Then Haystack decides what should happen next: whether the change can move forward, needs fixes, or should be reviewed by a human.

Teams use Haystack to keep code moving without turning review into rubber-stamping. It helps them merge more code, focus human attention on the changes that actually need judgment, and maintain quality as AI-generated work becomes a bigger part of development.
long_description.after:
Haystack automatically learns real customer journeys from production traffic, figures out which ones a code change could affect, and replays them in isolated copies of production to catch regressions before they ship.

When something breaks, Haystack shows exactly what changed across the UI, network calls, and events, then gives the failure back to your coding agent to fix and rerun. Teams get high-fidelity QA without having to write or maintain test cases.

one_liner.before: The agent-native control layer for code changes
one_liner.after: Replay real customer journeys against every change before you ship

long_description.before:
Post-order operations are one of the least automated parts of e-commerce. After an order is placed, teams still spend their days tracking shipments, chasing exceptions, processing returns, adjusting invoices, and answering “Can you check this?” requests. This manual busywork lives outside core systems and scales linearly with order volume, forcing brands and 3PLs to keep adding headcount as they scale.

Handled is an operations automation platform for e-commerce brands and the 3PLs that run their order fulfillment. We execute the manual work that happens after an order is placed by unifying post-order data across commerce, warehouse, carrier, and support systems.
Handled gives teams real-time visibility across orders, shipments, returns, and inventory in one system — eliminating the need to dig through disconnected tools or react only after customers complain. When issues occur, Handled automatically executes the follow-up work, such as resolving shipment delays, processing returns, filing claims, or making order and billing adjustments, without manual back-and-forth.

By combining visibility, issue detection, and automated execution in a single AI-powered operational layer, Handled replaces manual coordination with software-driven post-order operations in a large, recurring market tied directly to e-commerce volume.
long_description.after:
Consumer brands run finance and operations across ERPs, commerce platforms, 3PLs, accounting systems, email, and spreadsheets. Because these systems do not share context or complete work, teams still spend hours assembling reports, reconciling numbers, entering orders, monitoring inventory, processing invoices, and chasing exceptions. Problems are often discovered only after they have cost the business time, margin, or revenue.

Handled is an AI teammate for finance and operations. It connects to the systems and unstructured information a brand already uses and learns its data, rules, and workflows. Handled answers questions about the business, proactively catches issues, and takes on recurring manual work across financial reporting, inventory, procurement, wholesale order-to-cash, and AP/AR. It works across systems and brings a person in when judgment or approval is required.

Handled gives lean teams more operating capacity without adding another tool to manage, more outsourced support, or more headcount.

one_liner.before: Automating post-order operations for e-commerce brands and 3PLs
one_liner.after: AI teammate for finance and operations teams at consumer brands

long_description.before:
ThirdLayer is an applied research and product lab building the next interface for human–AI collaboration.

Our first product is Dex, an AI copilot for the browser. Think Cursor for knowledge work, optimized for speed and embedded directly where you work.

Most web agents are built for set-and-forget tasks. But real work is fluid and messy—spread across tabs, tools, and evolving decisions. Dex transforms your browser into an intelligent, multimodal workspace that understands your intent through voice, text, and action. It enhances familiar interfaces, automates tedious steps, and removes the friction of handoffs.

Beneath the surface, Dex is more than a browser agent — it’s a foundation for:

● Long-term, cross-modal memory grounded in real workflows
● A new interaction layer to replace static UI with a collaborative canvas 
● Personalization: understanding how individuals approach tasks and navigate software

We're building the infrastructure for adaptive, intent-aware systems that work the way you do.
long_description.after:
ThirdLayer is the learning and alignment layer for enterprise AI. We continuously ingest and structure messy organizational context, complex operational processes, and siloed, permission-sensitive data, then grade agents against the outcomes each company cares about. Every interaction becomes feedback that helps agents improve over time.

Companies use ThirdLayer to power their internal agents or embed it into the AI products they’re building. We give agents the context, evaluations, and learning loops they need to stay aligned with each organization and deliver better outcomes with every run.

long_description.before:
OS3 deploys US-built mobile semi humanoid robots for repetitive physical work.

We designed the robot, custom actuators, model and control stack as one system, then pretrained the model exclusively on 150,000 hours of video data spanning more than 2,000 tasks. Hospitality is our first deployment vertical. Through our Startup Partner program, teams are deploying OS3 robots in biotech, hospitals and data centers.

Our two-person team built 3 robots and trained its first model in four months. We are making American robotics accessible to more businesses.
long_description.after:
OS3 is building the platform that makes intelligent robots accessible to every business.

Today, robotics is constrained by two fundamental bottlenecks: hardware is too expensive to deploy at scale, and robots are difficult to train because high-quality robotics data is scarce and costly to collect. 

We built OS3 to solve both.

Our two-person team designed and a US-made mobile humanoid robot for a fraction of the cost of commercial alternatives. On the intelligence side, instead of relying on expensive robot-generated training data, we trained our own video-action model on 150,000 hours of real-world video spanning more than 2,000 tasks. Every deployed robot feeds new experience into our reinforcement learning pipeline, self improving robot fleet over time.

This creates a robot that can be deployed across industries to automate repetitive, physical work without requiring a new robot or training pipeline for every task. Our robots are already deployed in hotels, with customers now expanding the platform into biotech, hospitals, and data centers, including a wet lab at Stanford.

Our mission is to do for robotics what Apple did for personal computing: take technology that was once expensive, specialized, and inaccessible and make it powerful and usable at massive scale. We’re building toward a world with billions of intelligent robots, and OS3 is the platform that makes that possible.

one_liner.before: Deploying US-Built Humanoid Robots & Training Video Action Models
one_liner.after: Affordable, intelligent humanoid robots built to deploy at scale

long_description.before: Sidekick is an AI agent that manages manufacturing operations over text. Workers text problems, photos, or voice memos in any language; it answers from the company's own documents, creates and routes the work order, and syncs with the software the company already runs. No app, no login, works on any phone. It watches connected machine data and texts the right worker the moment something starts drifting, before it becomes downtime. And it compounds: most of the industrial world runs on undocumented knowledge, and Sidekick is the first thing that documents it as a byproduct of the work itself. Every interaction contributes to a searchable knowledge base the company owns, so tribal knowledge stops walking out the door when veterans retire.
long_description.after:
Sidekick is an AI agent that runs custom manufacturing operations over text. Workers text a problem, photo, video, or voice memo and get an answer from the shop's own documents. It reads live machine data and acts on its own: flagging issues before they become downtime, opening and routing work orders, and placing purchase orders. No app, no login.

These shops run on tribal knowledge: a handful of veterans know how every job is set up, and they are retiring. Sidekick learns from every message it handles, so answers outlive the people who gave them, and shops run 15% more jobs with the same crew. Sidekick captures it as a byproduct of the work, in an industry that was never documented.

long_description.before:
Dialogus builds voice agent infrastructure for enterprises.

Most companies can demo an AI voice agent, but getting one into production is hard. Enterprise agents need to connect to phone systems, internal tools, databases, CRMs, messaging channels, human escalation flows, monitoring, and compliance processes.

Dialogus provides the infrastructure to deploy production-grade voice agents that don’t just talk but complete real workflows. Our platform lets enterprises launch agents that collect information, validate it against internal systems, update records, send follow-up messages, and escalate edge cases to humans.
long_description.after:
Dialogus builds self-improving AI voice agents for enterprise operations.

Our agents handle high-volume workflows across customer support, sales, collections, and other operational functions, integrating directly with the systems enterprises already use.

Our agents continuously learn from real conversations and business outcomes: identifying where interactions fail, proposing improvements, testing those changes across thousands of simulated conversations, and deploying better versions with human oversight.

The result is AI that doesn’t just automate calls, it gets better at doing the job over time.

long_description.before:
Graphify builds a queryable knowledge graph from your codebase, docs, and Jira. The open-source engine has 105K+ GitHub stars and ~5M downloads, and is used in production by engineers at Rootly, Geotab, Tweddle Group, and Superagent.

On top of that graph, our enterprise layer reviews every pull request and formally verifies each code change: it proves the new behavior matches the old, or hands back the exact input that breaks it. That makes it built for the changes teams fear most, like refactors, framework upgrades, and large-scale code migrations, where you need proof that nothing broke, not a guess.

The graph updates itself as the code changes and keeps context instead of forgetting it, so your whole team and their coding agents work from one shared, always-current view of the codebase instead of a thousand private threads.

It runs entirely inside your perimeter, fully air-gapped on-premise or self-hosted in your own cloud, so no code or data ever leaves your environment.

long_description.before:
Nobody's built truly proactive AI, because it requires running inference on your entire life. In the cloud, that's insanely expensive and a privacy nightmare. But not on your own chip.

Every night, Sentient's on-device LLM wakes your Mac and understands what's new in your life (email, messages, files, Granola transcripts...), entirely locally, and distills it into a knowledge base.

You wake up to your work already prepared: the reply you forgot, drafted from your own context; the subscription you never use renewing tomorrow, caught; the report you promised in the group chat, ready to send. Everything is one click from firing through computer use, and nothing fires until you click.

Or click your Mac notch anytime and say "finish this for me." Sidekick takes over the thing you were doing with its own cursor while you move on.

On-device inference at this scale was supposed to be impossible: devices too slow, and models too dumb. So we built the stack ourselves: a custom LiteRT-LM fork (KV-cache reuse, speculative decoding, custom k-quants) that runs nightly on 8 GB Macs. The user's hardware does ~90% of the compute, and their own ChatGPT or Claude subscription does the rest, so our marginal cost is ~$0, and our servers store nothing.

We soft-launched late July with one Reddit post: top of r/macapps, 2,000+ users in 48 hours, $0 marketing. Free and open source for consumers; the same engine on the work stack (Slack, Granola, Linear, Notion) becomes the enterprise business.
